lead: A new matrix-multiplication manuscript makes an arithmetic-exponent claim, while a model-ranked problem directory makes its own uncertainty explicit. Small generative models, archival research and systems essays retain experimental and case-study limits; market reporting distinguishes estimates, transactions and forecasts.

sections.title: A claimed matrix exponent is not a verified practical runtime
sections.intro: Two feeds point to one OpenAI manuscript; exponent equality and tight Theta wording must remain separate.

sections.title: Model-ranked mathematical importance is not expert consensus
sections.intro: ProofAtlas discloses model weights, stale-fit diagnostics and limited dated status reviews.

sections.title: Stroke generation exposes the value and limits of training data
sections.intro: PenGPT separates selected visuals from random outputs and still struggles with binding and legibility.

sections.title: An archive lead and practitioner milestones remain case reports
sections.intro: A fuller historical account and Willison's retrospective do not establish universal autonomous research.

sections.title: Lock semantics and search-engine rewrites need workload-specific judgment
sections.intro: Ronacher proposes different poisoning defaults; Marginalia's incremental C++ experiment remains undecided.

sections.title: Disclosure estimates and IPO sales describe different financial events
sections.intro: Estimated holdings gains differ from realized IPO transactions, neither establishes motive.

sections.title: Asian market levels and HP guidance retain timestamp and accounting limits
sections.intro: Evolving session prices and adjusted profit forecasts are not closing results or guaranteed demand.
